Criminal Procedure Code (Amendment) Bill

bill · 8 March 2019 · 189 sentences in the record

Criminal Procedure Code (Amendment) Bill

159 of 189 sentences in this record
Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
CJRA criminal justice changes

The CJRA introduced video recording of interviews, a procedure to reopen exhausted criminal cases, and changes to evidence disclosure and sentencing powers.

  2. s00002 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

    CJRA introduced, amongst other things, the video recording of interviews in investigations and a statutory procedure for the reopening of criminal cases where all appeals had been exhausted.

  3. s00003 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

    Changes were also made to disclosure of evidence in criminal proceedings and to the sentencing powers of the Court, including to the sentence of Reformative Training.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    VRI offences and evidence redaction

    The Bill lets prescribed agencies investigate VRI-related offences and lets the Police or Prosecution redact sensitive information before disclosure.

    1. s00017 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      As such, the Bill will allow prescribed law enforcement agencies which already have the power to take VRI statements to investigate any VRI-related offences relating to the statements they take.

    3. s00019 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      The second amendment will allow the Police or the Prosecution to redact sensitive information from any document or thing relating to a criminal case before disclosing it to the Defence or other persons.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    Reformative Training backdating and minimum period

    An amendment proposes that RT sentences cannot be backdated, and the Court may set the minimum period at 12 or six months.

    1. s00046 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      An amendment is proposed to provide that an RT sentence cannot be backdated.

    2. s00047 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      What this means is that even if an offender was remanded before sentence, any RT sentence imposed cannot be backdated to take the remand period into account.

    4. s00049 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      The period used to be 18 months, but under those amendments, the Court is given the discretion to set the minimum period at either 12 months or six months depending on the nature of the rehabilitation required.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    Agencies minimising remand for RT

    The Police and Attorney-General's Chambers will work together to avoid or minimise remand where RT is a possible sentence.

    1. s00057 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      To address this, the relevant agencies, such as the Police and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC), will work together to ensure that where RT is a possible sentence, remand is either avoided or minimised where possible.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai · Ms Sylvia Lim
    Support with clarification requests

    The speaker moves the motion, supports the amendments, and asks the Ministry to clarify matters on VRIs and RT sentences.

    1. s00062 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Faicontext

      With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

    2. s00063 · 358Ms Sylvia Lim — Aljunied

      I am generally supportive of the amendments proposed, but I would like the Ministry to clarify two matters, firstly, relating to VRIs and, secondly, on RT sentences.

    • Ms Sylvia Lim
    VRI agency use and backdating removal

    The Minister is asked which agencies use VRI and for what offences, and Clause 6 removes the judge's right to backdate custody.

    1. s00070 · 358Ms Sylvia Lim — Aljunied

      To get a sense of how widespread the use of VRI is among our law enforcement agencies, could the Minister inform the House as to which agencies have commenced using VRI, and for what kinds of offences?

    3. s00072 · 358Ms Sylvia Lim — Aljunied

      Clause 6 of the Bill basically removes the right of the sentencing judge to backdate the period of custody to an earlier date.

    • Ms Sylvia Lim
    Avoiding or minimising remand

    The passage asks what practical steps will be taken to avoid or minimise remand, as MinLaw has stated.

    1. s00081 · 358Ms Sylvia Lim — Aljunied

      In order to avoid or minimise remand as MinLaw has stated, what practical things will be done?

    • Mr Christopher de Souza
    Investigating VRI-related offences

    Clause 3 of the Bill allows officers of prescribed law enforcement agencies to investigate offences relating to VRIs.

    1. s00084 · 358Mr Christopher de Souza — Holland-Bukit Timah

      In terms of investigations, clause 3 of the Bill allows officers of prescribed law enforcement agencies to investigate offences relating to VRIs.

    • Mr Christopher de Souza
    Non-disclosure of sensitive information

    Clause 9 provides for non-disclosure of sensitive information and a process for it, balancing the accused's rights with others' interests.

    1. s00090 · 358Mr Christopher de Souza — Holland-Bukit Timah

      Moving on to amendments relating to the pre-trial and trial stages, clause 9 provides for the non-disclosure of sensitive information and a process for it, that is, seeking a balance between the accused’s rights and interests with those of others.

    • Mr Christopher de Souza
    Removing backdating of RT

    Clause 6 removes the Courts' ability to backdate RT, which the High Court said could undermine the programme's effectiveness.

    1. s00105 · 358Mr Christopher de Souza — Holland-Bukit Timah

      Clause 6 removes the ability of the Courts to backdate RT.

    3. s00107 · 358Mr Christopher de Souza — Holland-Bukit Timah

      As the Singapore High Court in the case of Nur Azilah bte Ithnin vv Public Prosecutor opined, backdating RT will shorten the period of training and could undermine or hinder the effectiveness of such a programme.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    Training and inter-agency workgroup

    Agencies will assess needed training before bringing changes into force, overseen by an inter-agency workgroup for uniform VRI implementation.

    1. s00116 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Faicontext

      As with all legislative amendments, before bringing the changes into force, the relevant agencies will assess what kind of training or preparation is needed and will get that done.

    2. s00117 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      There is an inter-agency workgroup comprising the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), MinLaw, AGC, the Police and other law enforcement agencies which oversees the development of policies, operational procedures and also training plans to ensure uniformity in VRI implementation across the agencies.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    VRI use and feedback

    VRI has been used in rape and drug trafficking investigations, with useful feedback, but no VRI recording has yet been used as evidence in Court.

    1. s00125 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      VRI has been used by the Serious Sexual Crime Branch of the Criminal Investigation Department in investigations into rape, and by the Central Narcotics Bureau to investigate certain drug trafficking offences.

    3. s00127 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Faicontext

      Early feedback from the ground and from these agencies is that VRI is useful to investigators and our officers are confident in the VRI system.

    4. s00128 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      So far, there has not yet been a case where a VRI recording has been used as evidence in Court.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    Defence application without procedural barrier

    The Defence may apply for the Court's determination without any procedural barrier.

    1. s00136 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      The Defence may apply for the Court’s determination without any procedural barrier.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    Prosecution disclosure obligations and rebuttable presumption

    Courts set procedures balancing competing interests; the apex Court held the presumption of Prosecution compliance with disclosure obligations can be rebutted.

    1. s00150 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Faicontext

      The Courts have set down detailed procedures to fairly balance the competing interests in this area.

    2. s00151 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      And the High Court's decision in Winston Lee's case was then subsequently brought before the Court of Appeal in a Criminal Reference, and our apex Court stated that while the Public Prosecutor is presumed to have complied with his disclosure obligations on account of his constitutional office, this presumption can be rebutted.

    3. s00152 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      Once the Defence satisfies the Court that there are reasonable grounds for belief that the Prosecution has failed to comply with its Kadar obligation, the Court will look to the Prosecution to show that it has complied.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    RT sentence start date confirmation

    Ms Sylvia Lim asked for confirmation that a Court will not have an RT sentence take effect later than the date passed if the offender is in pre-sentence remand.

    1. s00177 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      Ms Sylvia Lim also asked for confirmation that a Court will not have an RT sentence take effect on a date later than the date it was passed if the offender is already in pre-sentence remand, as I understand the question.

    • Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
    CT for adult repeat offenders

    CT applies to adult repeat offenders with serious previous convictions, with sentences of five to 14 years and no remission entitlement.

    1. s00184 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      CT applies to adult offenders – as opposed to RT – who have committed one or more offences with maximum sentences of two years' imprisonment or more, and who also have relatively serious previous convictions.

    2. s00185 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      These adult repeat offenders can be sentenced to CT for a minimum of five and a maximum of 14 years, without entitlement to remission.

    3. s00186 · 358Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

      Considering the long minimum duration of CT sentences, there is less risk that backdating of such sentences will interfere with any rehabilitative efforts during the sentence.

    Ministries combining expertise on challenges

    Four Ministries came together on low-income families, MCI and economic agencies work on SME digital capabilities, and agencies partner on Industry Transformation Maps.

    1. s00034 · 1161Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

      To address inequality, no fewer than four Ministries have come together to ensure that we deliver practical solutions to help low-income families in Singapore.

    2. s00035 · 1161Ms Grace Fu Hai Yiencontext

      To help businesses navigate the digital future, Minister Iswaran shared how MCI and the economic agencies are working together to raise the digital capabilities of our small and medium enterprises.

    3. s00036 · 1161Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

      These follow from initiatives like the Industry Transformation Maps, where Government agencies partner one another to drive enterprise growth, support worker training, and address regulatory matters.

    4. s00037 · 1161Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

      In a complex world, combining our expertise, assets and strengths is the best way to overcome challenges.

    5. s00038 · 1161Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

      And our Public Service has the will and ability to do this.

    7. s00040 · 1161Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

      Our Nominated Members of Parliament (NMPs) who debuted this year deserve special mention.

    • Mr Speaker
    Merdeka Generation Package and universal schemes

    During this Committee of Supply, some have asked for more universal and permanent schemes when considering the Merdeka Generation Package.

    1. s00071 · 1161Mr Speaker

      When we consider, for example, the Merdeka Generation Package during this Committee of Supply (COS), some have asked for more universal and permanent schemes.

    • Mr Speaker
    Streaming changes and Minister Ong's explanation

    Streaming changes are much welcomed, but Minister Ong Ye Kung explained there was a reason for that cow.

    1. s00079 · 1161Mr Speaker

      Streaming changes are much welcomed but, as Minister Ong Ye Kung explained, there was a reason for that cow.

    • Mr Speaker
    Election timing and balanced Budget

    The speaker does not know when the election will be, but the Constitution requires a balanced Budget over each Government term.

    1. s00088 · 1161Mr Speakercontext

      Honestly, I have no idea when the election will be.

    2. s00089 · 1161Mr Speaker

      But what I do know is that our Constitution requires us to maintain a balanced Budget over each term of Government.

    3. s00090 · 1161Mr Speaker

      Towards the end of each term, we have better clarity of the overall Budget and how it affords us the space to carry out strategic moves if we need them.

    • Mr Speaker
    Merdeka Generation Package and election Budget

    The speaker says if this were an election Budget, the Merdeka Generation Package would not be left unbudgeted.

    1. s00093 · 1161Mr Speaker

      Honestly, if this were an election Budget, you will not see us not budgeting for the Merdeka Generation Package here.

    • Mr Speaker
    Dominance, spending and prudence

    A politically astute government would use its dominance to justify more spending rather than talk of prudence, balance, tradeoffs and possible GST increases.

    1. s00096 · 1161Mr Speaker

      A politically astute government would use this dominance and wherewithal to justify even more spending rather than still talk about prudence, about balance, about tradeoffs, possible Goods and Services Tax increases in the next term.

    • Mr Speaker
    False news erodes trust

    False and fake news erode trust and confidence and undermine leaders and institutions, including Parliament.

    1. s00105 · 1161Mr Speakercontext

      We talk about false and fake news impacting perceptions.

    2. s00106 · 1161Mr Speaker

      This is really not trivial at all because they erode trust, they erode confidence and, ultimately, they undermine leaders and institutions, including Parliament.

    • Mr Speaker
    Parliament relevance, trust and mandate

    The speaker urges continued robust discourse and says only a relevant, trusted and respected Parliament will be afforded space and mandate to lead.

    1. s00116 · 1161Mr Speakercontext

      I urge you to continue in this vein and for the Government to be open as it has been to this robust discourse.

    2. s00117 · 1161Mr Speaker

      It is only if we, as a Parliament, can remain relevant, trusted and respected, will our people afford us that space and mandate to lead and chart the way forward.
